# Ridu 0.17.0

SvelteKit applications can now let their users write rich text with the editor the admin uses, and
Ridu's Svelte packages ship as ordinary compiled Svelte libraries.

## Changes

- `@riducms/plugin-richtext/editor` exports `RichTextEditor`, which edits a `richtext.Field` value
  in an application. It needs no Vite plugin, preprocessing, Sass, or admin runtime. Bind it to the
  field's value and save that value through the generated client; pass the same `features` as the
  Go field, and every edit passes the field's validation.
- The editor renders with SvelteKit's server rendering: the server shows the saved document with
  the editor's styles, and the browser swaps in the editor without moving the page.
- `toolbar` places the formatting controls over a selection, above the text, or both, and the
  admin's layout options (`hideGutter` and the block controls) are props. `lang`, `dir`, and
  `messages` translate it; it includes English, French, and Arabic.
- The editor's colors, fonts, and main sizes are `--ridu-richtext-*` custom properties. The
  defaults follow the admin theme, or an application theme that uses shadcn-style names such as
  `--foreground` and `--border`, and fall back to a neutral light theme. Sass users can configure
  the defaults with `@use "@riducms/plugin-richtext/editor.scss" with (...)`. The admin looks the
  same as in 0.16.2.
- On touch screens, toolbar buttons and menu options are 44 pixels, and a fixed toolbar stays in view
  while the on-screen keyboard is open.
- The new [Use the editor in your app](https://riducms.com/docs/rich-text/editor/) guide covers
  installation, saving, translation, styling, server rendering, and phones.
- Ridu's Svelte packages (`@riducms/ui`, `@riducms/plugin`, the official admin plugins, and
  `@riducms/sveltekit`) follow the `sv create` library template and publish `svelte-package` output
  in `dist`. Their component stylesheets are compiled to CSS, so applications need no Sass, and
  `@riducms/translations` publishes compiled JavaScript, so applications can import
  `@riducms/plugin` during server rendering.
- With `TabbedUI`, the SEO plugin shows one tab bar with Content and SEO, instead of two tab bars
  where selecting SEO didn't hide the content.
- Menus and popovers no longer cause a Svelte `derived_inert` warning in development when they open
  and close quickly, after an upgrade to Bits UI 2.19.5.
- Ridu uses `golang.org/x/text` v0.41.0, which fixes a panic on crafted input in its `precis`
  package ([GO-2026-6629](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6629)). `govulncheck` found it
  reachable from the admin's search parameter decoding.

## Breaking changes and upgrade

Update the Go module and all Ridu npm packages to 0.17.0 together, regenerate application contracts,
and rebuild the admin and application binary. This release changes no Go APIs, authoring config,
manifest or protocol versions, REST or SDK behavior, migration planners, or database layouts, so
existing databases and migration histories need no changes.

- Ridu's Svelte packages export only their compiled `dist`. Imports of their `src` paths, or of the
  `@ui/*`, `@plugin-richtext/*`, and `@plugin-seo/*` aliases, must use the packages' public exports.
- `@riducms/build` no longer exports `createAdminLibraryConfig`.
- Generated admins no longer need the `@ui/*`, `@plugin-richtext/*`, and `@plugin-seo/*` paths in
  `admin/tsconfig.json`, the Lexical preprocessing in `admin/vite.config.ts`, or the
  `@hvniel/lexical-svelte` dependency in `admin/package.json`. They no longer do anything; remove
  them. New projects don't have them.
- Admin plugins keep their contract. `@riducms/ui` and `@riducms/admin` require Bits UI 2.19.5, and
  `@riducms/plugin-richtext` adds `esm-env` as a dependency.

This is a pre-1 release with breaking contracts; keep the coordinated packages aligned. Production
still runs as a Go binary with its static admin embedded, without a JavaScript server.
